section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1993
title: ACCIDENTAL DEATHS & SUICIDES IN INDIA - 1993 N.C.R.B.- 16 1.3.4 Approximately one-fourth of the total ‘Accidental Deaths’ were reported due to ‘Road Accidents’ during the year, a large majority (91%) of which were due to motor vehicle mishaps. TABLE-3.1 presents the distribution of ‘Motor Vehicles Deaths’ and their rate of occurrence in various States/UTs during the years 1992 & 1993. It is interesting to note that although the number of Motor Vehicles increased by 10.3 per cent in the country during 1992 and by another 7.6 per cent in 1993, the rate of ‘Accidental Deaths’ per thousand ‘Motor Vehicles’ surprisingly decreased by 2.2 and 7.8 per cent respectively during the same period. Contrary to expectations, the highest rate of deaths was reported from hill states of Himachal Pradesh (4.47) and Meghalaya (4.07) which was more than double the National average. The comparatively higher growth in the number of vehicles in the country has, no doubt, contributed to the decline in the above rate of motor vehicle accidents. However other highly correlated factors like growing safety consciousness amongst drivers and pedestrians in obeying traffic regulations, increased electrification and better conditions of the roads, hi-technology checks using computerised periscope vans, radar guns, video traffic monitors etc. coupled with more intensive and extensive monitoring of the vehicular movements by the traffic police are expected to have contributed in the reduction of the accident rate.
